llm.summary: This skill does what it claims, but it sends project code to a remote compile server and can flash unverified firmware while disabling TLS certificate checks.

dimensions.detail: The helper zips and uploads the project to a user-selected server, downloads firmware components from that server, and may flash a device; these are purpose-aligned but high-impact and not sufficiently protected by certificate validation or artifact verification.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains a skill file, helper scripts, docs, and a small agent metadata file; I found no hidden installer, obfuscation, or unrelated startup behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The workflow repeatedly uses insecure TLS bypasses (`curl -k`/`-sk`) and troubleshooting docs normalize certificate-warning bypasses without enough identity-verification guidance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No agent persistence is installed, but the documented self-hosted server may run under systemd/Docker and flashing writes persistent firmware to a connected K10; this is disclosed and central to the workflow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Remote compilation, firmware download, Web Serial flashing, server-side flashing, and optional local esptool upload all fit the stated K10 compile-server purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the compile server and network path. Prefer a LAN/VPN server with proper certificates or pinned identity, avoid public unauthenticated exposure, and understand that server-side/local flashing can overwrite the connected K10 firmware. Review cleanup and erase commands before copying them.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Shell commands and helper scripts are expected for this developer hardware workflow, and the commands are visible in the artifact; this supports guidance rather than an independent malicious finding.
[SQP-2] expected: Flashing, cleanup, certificate-bypass, erase, and serial-permission troubleshooting are related to the stated purpose, but the docs under-warn about destructive or trust-weakening consequences.
[SC2] expected: Uploading source to a compile server and downloading firmware are core behavior, but using TLS verification bypasses and lacking firmware integrity checks makes this a material Review concern.
